disclosure: Authored adoption assumptions for discovery, not a certified maturity model or an assessed client. Technology names are examples. Unknown prerequisites remain gaps; no average score can override a missing requirement.

dependencies.title: Requirements & expected outcomes
dependencies.assumption: Approved requirements, representative defects and independent expected results are available for the selected journey.
dependencies.evidence: A versioned scenario with source links, accepted edge cases and a named reviewer; a deliberately incorrect result is rejected.
dependencies.action: Resolve ambiguous payment rules and record the test oracle before generating assertions.
dependencies.example: Azure Boards, Test Plans and a reviewed scenario catalog
dependencies.harbor: PAY-142 exists; product owners must confirm retry, concurrency and journal rules.

dependencies.title: Infrastructure & environments
dependencies.assumption: A permitted cloud or on-premises environment can run the application and tests with sufficient capacity, network routes, credentials and isolation.
dependencies.evidence: Another engineer provisions or restores the pinned build, completes health checks and records reset time and runner capacity.
dependencies.action: Resolve runner access, image or package access, deployment drift and environment booking before execution.
dependencies.example: Existing Azure environment and pipeline agents; infrastructure as code where supported
dependencies.harbor: A shared Azure test environment exists; independent reset and concurrent capacity are unproven.

dependencies.title: DevOps & delivery pipelines
dependencies.assumption: Builds, tests, deployments and configuration are versioned and can be repeated without undocumented manual steps.
dependencies.evidence: A run links the commit, build, deployment, test and configuration revisions; a failed required test stops promotion.
dependencies.action: Create a reproducible pipeline and retain mandatory suites before AI recommends test selection.
dependencies.example: Azure Pipelines or GitHub Actions; existing repositories and artifact stores
dependencies.harbor: CI is available; deployment remains partly manual and artifact links need integration.

dependencies.title: Service virtualization & dependencies
dependencies.assumption: External APIs, callbacks, messages and legacy or batch dependencies have an explicit test strategy: controlled substitutes where suitable and scheduled real integration checks.
dependencies.evidence: Versioned contracts and scenarios reproduce success, timeout, duplicate and delayed responses; a provider check detects drift from the real integration.
dependencies.action: Inventory protocols and owners, agree stub fidelity and refresh triggers, and book a sandbox or batch window for what cannot be simulated.
dependencies.example: WireMock for HTTP behavior; Pact where applicable for contracts; protocol-specific simulators for messages or legacy systems
dependencies.harbor: Provider stubs are proposed work. The shared settlement batch and real provider sandbox still need reserved validation windows.

dependencies.title: Test data & reset
dependencies.assumption: Permitted synthetic or appropriately controlled data preserves business relationships and can be isolated and reset per run.
dependencies.evidence: Two runs start from known balances and relationships without interfering; data use, cleanup and reset duration are recorded.
dependencies.action: Create deterministic fixtures and unique test accounts. Review data handling before model or runner access.
dependencies.example: PostgreSQL seed fixtures; Testcontainers for bounded service tests with a compatible runtime
dependencies.harbor: Synthetic account fixtures and scripted reset are backlog items; shared records cannot establish repeatability.

dependencies.title: Application & integration testability
dependencies.assumption: The chosen application exposes controllable interfaces and observable outcomes; web, mobile and legacy constraints are assessed separately.
dependencies.evidence: A retry can be injected and its transfer identity, journal count and balances inspected; batch and asynchronous completion are observable.
dependencies.action: Add test hooks, stable interfaces and outcome access, or narrow the pilot to an independently testable component.
dependencies.example: Java payment APIs, React web, existing mobile app and a separately scheduled settlement batch
dependencies.harbor: Payment APIs are the candidate surface. UI reliability and batch independence are not assumed to match API readiness.

dependencies.title: Frameworks, runners & devices
dependencies.assumption: Owned test suites provide meaningful assertions, dependable fixtures and the required API, web, mobile and nonfunctional coverage.
dependencies.evidence: Tests catch an injected defect, reruns expose flakiness, and the selected browsers, devices and operating systems are available.
dependencies.action: Stabilize seed tests and ownership; retain required coverage while evaluating generated tests and maintenance suggestions.
dependencies.example: JUnit / REST Assured, Playwright, existing Selenium and Appium; current performance tooling
dependencies.harbor: Some Java tests are usable; noisy UI tests and device scheduling require their own readiness decisions.

dependencies.title: Observability & release evidence
dependencies.assumption: Runner results, logs, traces, defects and release records are accessible, correlated and retained for the intended review.
dependencies.evidence: A failure can be traced from requirement and build to the original assertion, environment state, defect decision and fresh retest.
dependencies.action: Connect run IDs and artifacts; distinguish product, environment and test faults before AI triage is trusted.
dependencies.example: Pipeline artifacts, Playwright traces, OpenTelemetry signals and Azure Boards
dependencies.harbor: Evidence is spread across tools; a joined run manifest and retention rules must be demonstrated.

dependencies.title: AI access, data rules & evaluation
dependencies.assumption: The model and connectors are approved for the intended inputs, identities, locations and actions, with usable limits and human review.
dependencies.evidence: Approved input boundaries, an access test, representative evaluation cases, model/prompt versions, spend limits and a safe disable path.
dependencies.action: Confirm endpoint availability, permitted context, residency/retention requirements, licensing and action scope before connecting client assets.
dependencies.example: The client's approved model endpoint or coding assistant; selected versioned context before retrieval expansion
dependencies.harbor: An approved endpoint and permission to use repository context are assumptions to validate, not installed capabilities.

dependencies.title: People, skills & offshore handoffs
dependencies.assumption: Domain reviewers, developers and platform engineers have allocated time, access and skills; supplier incentives support reuse and quality.
dependencies.evidence: An offshore engineer submits a reviewable artifact and the named next owner accepts it within an agreed review window.
dependencies.action: Provide repository and environment access, pair coaching, escalation paths and funded review time across time zones.
dependencies.example: A pilot pod drawn from the assumed 75 QA staff, with additional product, development and platform support
dependencies.harbor: Domain expertise exists; automation skills and working-hour overlap are uneven. Support effort is additional to the eight QA pilot roles.

dependencies.title: Shared platform ownership & service capacity
dependencies.assumption: Reusable connectors, templates, data and runner services have an owner, support model, version policy and capacity for onboarding teams.
dependencies.evidence: For a pilot, demonstrate an owned service with usable capacity and reviewed versions. For scale, a second team onboards without the pilot authors; support, upgrade, license and concurrency limits are tested and budgeted.
dependencies.action: Name the service owner and first support boundary; sequence adoption by capacity rather than enabling every team at once.
dependencies.example: A supported QA service catalog over the existing stack; Kubernetes and a vector database are optional design choices
dependencies.harbor: A shared QA service is proposed. Cross-team reuse and support coverage have not been demonstrated.

dependencies.title: Baseline, funding & adoption evidence
dependencies.assumption: Comparable baseline work, foundation effort, recurring costs and intended use of released capacity are agreed before benefits are claimed.
dependencies.evidence: A sampled release pack separates active work, waiting, review, rework, setup, platform operation and license/model costs.
dependencies.action: Fund and schedule dependency remediation. Re-estimate the pilot when prerequisites change; separate automation gains from AI contribution.
dependencies.example: The Northstar Payments effort model is illustrative; no client savings rate or fixed adoption date is inferred
dependencies.harbor: The 300-hour baseline, 480-hour setup and 12-hour operating allowance are unverified planning assumptions, not a readiness budget.

workflows.output: Evidence-linked diagnosis and independently verified retest

workflows.output: A reviewed summary of results, gaps and owner decisions

sources.title: DORA: Test automation
sources.use: Fast, reliable suites and shared developer/tester responsibility inform the framework and ownership assumptions.

sources.title: DORA: Loosely coupled teams
sources.use: Independent testing, dependency control and explicit service contracts inform the infrastructure and integration design.

sources.title: WireMock: Service virtualization
sources.use: HTTP stubs can model state, delay and faults. The fidelity checks and real-integration gate here are authored requirements.

sources.title: Testcontainers: Container runtime requirements
sources.use: Testcontainers requires a compatible container runtime; it is not a substitute for provisioning the complete application estate.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Signals
sources.use: Telemetry signals inform the evidence integration design; instrumentation alone does not establish a correct financial outcome.

sources.title: Pact: Introduction to contract testing
sources.use: Consumer and provider interaction checks support compatibility; they do not replace end-to-end business-outcome tests.
